primary_meaning: The vulnerable, helpless, and marginalized who stand under God's special protective care and fatherhood, and whose defense is a mark of true righteousness and pure religion

alternatives.meaning: Spiritual condition of those without God as Father, or of disciples temporarily left without the immediate presence of Christ until the Spirit is given
Israel or God's covenant people in seasons of exile, judgment, or apparent abandonment
Allegorical type of the soul or the Church dependent on divine adoption rather than earthly lineage
basis: patristic and medieval allegorical readings of the Psalms and prophetic texts

notes: Consensus is strong on the ethical-theological force of the figure (God's character as father-protector and the corresponding duty of justice) rather than on any single elaborate allegory; the spiritual-adoption reading is also widespread in Christian teaching but secondary to the dominant social-justice and divine-care motif drawn from the Old Testament.
